title: Effective Edge-wise Representation Learning in Edge-Attributed Bipartite Graphs

problem.claim: Existing graph representation learning primarily generates node representations, which are not readily usable for edge-based analytics in edge-attributed bipartite graphs.

gap.claim: Limited research addresses edge representation learning in edge-attributed bipartite graphs, and existing workarounds reportedly achieve sub-par results.

contributions.claim: The paper designs EAGLE, an edge representation learning method for edge-attributed bipartite graphs.
It proposes factorized feature propagation to incorporate long-range dependencies of edges and features without tremendous computation overheads.
It extends factorized feature propagation into a dual-view scheme that separately accounts for influences from the two heterogeneous node sets.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on five real datasets evaluate the EAGLE models in semi-supervised edge classification tasks.
The authors report that EAGLE achieves gains of up to 38.11% in AP and 1.86% in AUC over the best baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph representation learning encodes graph elements into vector representations for downstream graph-data analysis.
Node-focused methods do not directly support edge-based analytics in edge-attributed bipartite graphs.
Edge representation learning must combine edge structure and attribute semantics while accounting for two heterogeneous node sets, an area with limited prior work.
The paper introduces EAGLE, factorized feature propagation, and a dual-view extension for edge representation learning.
The authors report results from five real datasets and gains over baselines in AP and AUC.

source_observation.claim: Edge representation learning in bipartite graphs needs to account separately for the influences of the two heterogeneous node sets.

interpretation.claim: When relational data has asymmetric or heterogeneous sides, modeling each side's influence separately may better preserve task-relevant structure.

application.claim: Consider separate-view or side-specific representations for edge prediction in user-item, customer-product, or user-merchant graphs.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether separate views help outside edge-attributed bipartite graphs or tasks beyond semi-supervised edge classification.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the five datasets.
The abstract does not specify the experimental splits, implementation details, or baseline methods.
The abstract does not provide the theoretical assumptions or analysis details.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
